children: shares fell 1.96% to 1,098,000 won at the November 17 regular-session close in Seoul, after a US federal judge declined to dismiss a proposed class action accusing it, Samsung Electronics and Micron of choking DRAM supply. The Kospi lost 2.59% as foreign investors sold heavily ahead of Nvidia's earnings.

Judge Noel Wise's November 14 order found the complaint adequately pleads a Sherman Act conspiracy and rejected the argument that it reruns an earlier DRAM case. The complaint, which TrendForce summarized on November 16, alleges production cuts and DDR4 phase-outs pushed DRAM prices up as much as 500% in a year. Defendants must answer by December 7, and the first case management conference is set for January 12, 2027.

For a company closely tied to high-bandwidth memory, the court's view that the HBM shift alone does not imply collusion narrows the attack on its most strategic product line. GuruFocus gives SK hynix a GF Score of 99/100, near the ceiling, powered by top-tier profitability and a strong balance sheet. Its GF Value of 1,425,428 won implies a 23% discount, which GuruFocus calls modestly undervalued. That gap already prices in plenty of fear, but it may not close until discovery limits are set in January and Nvidia confirms memory demand tonight.

title: SK hynix Stocks Fall 1.96% as DRAM Price-Fixing Suit Advances and Kospi Drops
